findings.message: The hardcoded fallback JSON string (jq-failure path) omits `exit_code`, `test_output`, and `run_mode` at the top level, so any consumer relying on the new top-level fields (asserted by SPEC-3/4/7) receives null from the fallback path, making the fallback output inconsistent with the v2 contract the primary write path now satisfies.

SPEC-8 joins two unrelated assertions with a pipe-delimiter (`"interrupted|true"` vs `"${_spec8_term}|${_spec8_has_to}"`): if only one sub-check fails the error message cannot identify which, and the `has("test_output")` half duplicates SPEC-1's check on the same artifact without adding coverage.

SPEC-3 and SPEC-4 each issue two `assert_eq` calls under the same label prefix (e.g. both `[SPEC-3]` lines), so when a runner reports failures by label, both assertions are indistinguishable and the specific failing sub-check (exit_code vs disposition) is hidden.
